clue.text: 10 23, solvers' bequests

definitions.meaning: the entries at 10 and 23 together name a Shakespeare comedy, and its alternative title is the phrase wanted
what solvers leave in their wills: whatever they choose to bequeath, addressed to 'you' the solver

explanation.walkthrough: The play at 10 23 has a subtitle of three words; the same words, read as 'that which you bequeath in your will', fit the second half.
explanation.definitionFit: The comedy's full title adds this phrase as its alternative name, and a will is where one leaves bequests.

clue.text: Hoists terrific lot with the Spanish gun

annotationWithheld.why: Hoists terrific lot with the Spanish gun (10,5): WINCHES + TERRIF + LE would need 'terrific lot' to give TERRIF and 'the Spanish' to give LE (Spanish 'the' is EL); no fair parse found and no blog located
annotationWithheld.clue: Hoists terrific lot with the Spanish gun

clue.text: Backer in the wings?

definitions.meaning: a financial backer of a theatre production
a being equipped with wings, with a nod to the wings of a theatre stage

explanation.definitionFit: In theatre slang a show's financial backer is called by the name of a winged heavenly messenger.

clue.text: Homework upset handsome man, hence the language

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the word is turned upside down, read from the bottom

parts.note: DIY, do-it-yourself, is home improvement work
a dish is slang for an attractive person

explanation.surface: Someone's botched home improvements upset a good-looking man, who switched languages.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' turns the home-improvement abbreviation upside down; 'hence' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The historic vernacular of Ashkenazi Jews, a Germanic tongue written in Hebrew script.

clue.text: Nervous or disapproving? Leave your bed and get drunk

parts.note: to get up is to leave your bed
tight is informal for drunk

explanation.surface: Advice to a jittery or prim person: get out of bed and get drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal adjective covers both being tense and anxious and being primly conventional and disapproving.

clue.text: I unexpectedly echo the custom of cold storage

indicators.note: something happening unexpectedly comes out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: use means custom or habitual practice

explanation.surface: Someone suddenly repeats the tradition of keeping things cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpectedly' scrambles the first two words; 'cold storage' names a building, with 'the' and 'of' as links.
explanation.definitionFit: An icehouse was a building for storing ice through the year, an early form of chilled storage.

clue.text: She-canine hid abode — futility shown here

definitions.text: She-canine hid abode — futility shown here

indicators.note: the letters of the preceding words are displayed here in a new arrangement, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A female dog conceals her kennel, which shows how pointless everything is.
explanation.walkthrough: All twenty-five letters of SHE-CANINE HID ABODE FUTILITY are rearranged, signalled by 'shown here'; the cynical saying is itself an expression of futility, so the whole clue defines.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying is a weary proverb summing up the pointlessness of existence, so it expresses futility.

clue.text: Worthies with a whole bag for rumination

parts.note: OM, the Order of Merit, is an honour held by national worthies
a sum is a whole or total

explanation.surface: Distinguished people carry a large bag in which to ponder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rumination' looks like deep thought but here means chewing the cud.
explanation.definitionFit: The omasum is the third stomach chamber of a ruminant, a pouch used in digesting cud.

clue.text: Psychotherapist's contract

definitions.meaning: slang name for a psychiatrist or therapist, from head-shrinker
to get smaller or draw back

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a therapist (from head-shrinker), and a verb meaning to become smaller.

clue.text: The other way the old chap ran

indicators.note: the phrase 'the old chap' has its two parts put the other way round

parts.note: a chap is a man
old means aged

explanation.surface: The old fellow ran off in the opposite direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the old chap' gives AGED MAN; 'The other way' swaps the order to MAN AGED.
explanation.definitionFit: To run a business or project is to manage it, so ran is the past tense synonym.

clue.text: Not the 21 23 of the play

parts.note: 21 and 23 together make an opening performance; the play meant is a Shakespeare comedy named after a later evening of Christmas festivities

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a later performance rather than the premiere; the answer is the Shakespeare title naming the last evening of the Christmas season.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shakespeare comedy is named for the twelfth evening after Christmas, which is plainly not an opening performance.

clue.text: Money makes society dreadful

parts.note: chilling means frightening or dreadful

explanation.surface: Cash produces a society that is frightening.
explanation.definitionFit: The schilling was the currency unit of Austria before the euro.

clue.text: Buck keeping wife within call

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: Oi! is a call to attract attention
a rib is a jocular word for a wife, from Adam's rib

explanation.surface: A man keeps his wife within shouting distance.
explanation.walkthrough: Rib for wife comes from Eve being made from Adam's rib; 'within' is a link beside 'keeping'.
explanation.definitionFit: The oribi is a small African antelope, and a male antelope is called a buck.

clue.text: Man's first question: what to put on one's face?

definitions.text: what to put on one's face?

indicators.note: first means take only the opening letter of the word Man's

parts.note: to ask is to question

explanation.surface: A man's first query is how to make himself up.
explanation.definitionFit: A mask is a covering worn over the face, the thing you put on it.

clue.text: Man-eater, a little bit upset — he's on an old ship

parts.note: a whit is a very small amount, as in 'not a whit'

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters of he's are rearranged

parts.note: he's is the contraction of he is, giving three letters
Noah's ark is the old ship

explanation.surface: A man-eater is somewhat upset to find itself on an ancient vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges HES to ESH; 'a' and 'on' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The great white shark is notorious for attacks on humans, so it is a classic man-eater.

clue.text: The ray is possibly not the controlling factor

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A ray probably is not the factor in control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges THE RAY IS into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hysteria is a state of uncontrolled emotion, the very opposite of being in control.

clue.text: See 6
Snob nose?

parts.note: a snob is said to be '___-nosed' with a sweet as the missing word, so the snob's nose is made of that sweet

explanation.definitionFit: Snobbish people are called toffee-nosed in British slang, so the sweet is the snob's nose.

clue.text: Wretched bun cooked in case

indicators.note: cooked means altered or fiddled, so the letters of bun are rearranged

parts.note: lest means in case or for fear that

explanation.surface: A miserable bun was baked just in case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' looks like baking but here means fiddled, so the bun's letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Unblest means unhappy or cursed, without blessing, hence wretched.

clue.text: Jaundiced view of English critic

indicators.note: a view of something presents it in another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A critic from England takes a sour view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'view of' rearranges E plus CRITIC; 'Jaundiced' looks like 'cynical' but is the medical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Icteric is the medical adjective for having jaundice, from icterus, the yellowing of the skin.

clue.text: 14, say, in brief, is hunted

annotationWithheld.why: 14, say, in brief, is hunted (4): '14, say' (a shark) defines FISH, but no fair reading of 'in brief, is hunted' gives the letters F, IS, H that has been found

clue.text: Rock salt — draw round it

indicators.note: round means placed around, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: hale is an old verb meaning to drag or draw

explanation.surface: Instructions to sketch a circle around some salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draw' is not sketching but the old verb hale, to haul.
explanation.definitionFit: Halite is the mineral name for natural sodium chloride, known as rock salt.

clue.text: No. 1 Conifer Street

parts.note: a fir is a cone-bearing tree

explanation.surface: It reads like an address: number one, Conifer Street.
explanation.definitionFit: Number one is the top position, the one ranked ahead of all others.

clue.text: Sort of gardens unfamiliar to Caliban

indicators.note: unfamiliar means made strange, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some gardens would be strange to Shakespeare's island monster Caliban.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfamiliar' rearranges TO CALIBAN; Caliban is the wild islander in The Tempest.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanical gardens display plants for study, so the adjective names a sort of garden.

clue.text: See 10
Make compulsory letter for the church

parts.note: en is the spelt-out name of the letter N
taken as written
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A letter makes something obligatory for church members.
explanation.definitionFit: To enforce a rule is to compel observance of it, making it mandatory.

clue.text: Don't start having a baby when on the throne

indicators.note: don't start means leave out the opening letter

parts.note: pregnant means expecting a baby

explanation.surface: Advice not to start a family while reigning.
explanation.definitionFit: Regnant means reigning, as in a queen regnant who rules in her own right.

clue.text: Happy about wine and coke, given a spring

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the others

parts.note: elated means very happy
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine
C is short for cocaine, of which coke is slang

explanation.surface: A cheerful drinker on wine and cocaine gets a bounce in the step.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given a spring' means fitted with elastic, not cheered up.
explanation.definitionFit: Elasticated fabric has elastic threads woven in, giving it springiness.
